nodes.statement: Note that our proposed setup only considers a single burst erasure during the entire duration of communication. nodes.statement: The proof of Lemma~ follows by observing that the capacity region for the problem in Fig.~(a) depends on the joint distribution p(mathssfs_j, mathssfs_j+1, mathssfs_j-1,mathssfs_j-B-1) only via the marginal distributions p(mathssfs_j, mathssfs_j-1) and p(mathssfs_j+1, mathssfs_j, mathssfs_j-B-1). Indeed the decoding error at decoder j depends on the former whereas the decoding error at decoder j+1 depends on the latter. When the source is symmetric, the joint distributions p(mathssfs_j, mathssfs_j-1) and p(mathssfs_j, mathssfs_j+1) are identical and thus exchanging mathssfs_j-1^n with mathssfs_j+1^n does not change the error probability at decoder j and leaves the functions at all other terminals unchanged. The formal proof is straightforward and will be omitted. Thus it suffices to lower bound the achievable sum-rate for the problem in Fig.~(b). First note that nR_j+1&= H(mathssff_j+1)notag\\ &ge I(mathssff_j+1 ;mathssfs_j+1^n | mathssfs^n_j-B-1, mathssff_j)notag\\ &= H(mathssfs_j+1^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j) -H(mathssfs_j+1^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j, mathssff_j+1)notag\\ &ge H(mathssfs_j+1^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j) - nvarepsilon_n where follows by applying Fano's inequality for decoder j+1 in Fig.~(b) since mathssfs_j+1^n can be recovered from (mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j, mathssff_j+1). To bound R_j &nR_j= H(mathssff_j)notag\\ &ge I(mathssff_j;mathssfs^n_j|mathssfs_j-B-1^n)nonumber \\ &= H(mathssfs_j^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n)notag - H(mathssfs_j^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j)nonumber \\ &ge nH(mathssfs_j|mathssfs_j-B-1)- H(mathssfs_j^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j) notag\\ & +H(mathssfs_j^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n,mathssfs_j+1^n, mathssff_j)-nvarepsilon_n\\ &=nH(mathssfs_j|mathssfs_j-B-1) - I(mathssfs_j^n; mathssfs_j+1^n |mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j)-nvarepsilon_nnonumber\\ &=nH(mathssfs_j|mathssfs_j-B-1)-H(mathssfs_j+1^n |mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j) notag\\ & + H( mathssfs_j+1^n |mathssfs_j-B-1^n,mathssfs_j^n, mathssff_j)-nvarepsilon_nnonumber\\ &=nH(mathssfs_j|mathssfs_j-B-1)-H(mathssfs_j+1^n |mathssfs_j-B-1^n, mathssff_j) notag\\ & + nH(mathssfs_j+1|mathssfs_j) -nvarepsilon_n where~ follows by applying Fano's inequality for decoder j in Fig.~(b) since mathssfs_j^n can be recovered from (mathssfs_j+1^n, mathssff_j) and hence H(mathssfs_j^n|mathssfs_j-B-1^n,mathssfs_j+1^n, mathssff_j) le nvarepsilon_n holds and~ follows from the Markov relation mathssfs_j+1^n rightarrow mathssfs_j^n rightarrow (mathssff_j, mathssfs_j-B-1^n). By summing~ and~ and using R_j=R_j+1=R, we have R_j+R_j+1 &ge H(mathssfs_j+1|mathssfs_j) + H(mathssfs_j|mathssfs_j-B-1) \\ &= H(mathssfs_j,mathssfs_j+1|mathssfs_j-B-1). which is equivalent to~.

nodes.statement: Since the underlying random variables are jointly Gaussian, we can express the MMSE estimates of mathssfs_t-k from W_j, jin\1,2\ as follows (see e.g. ) &hatmathssfs_t-k(W_1) = alpha_1 mathssfs_t-k +mathssfe_1 \\ &hatmathssfs_t-k(W_2) = alpha_2 mathssfs_t-k +mathssfe_2 where mathssfe_1 sim N(0, E_1) and mathssfe_2 sim N(0, E_2) are Gaussian random variables both independent of mathssfs_t-k. Furthermore the constants in~ and~ are given by &alpha_j = 1-sigma^2_t-k(W_j)\\ & E_j = sigma^2_t-k(W_j)(1-sigma^2_t-k(W_j)) for j=1,2. To establish~, we have h(mathssfs_t | W_1, mathbsfu_Omega) &= h(mathssfs_t | hatmathssfs_t-k(W_1), mathbsfu_Omega)\\ & = h(mathssfs_t | alpha_1 mathssfs_t-k +mathssfe_1, mathbsfu_Omega) \\ & le h(mathssfs_t | alpha_2 mathssfs_t-k +mathssfe_2, mathbsfu_Omega) \\ &= h(mathssfs_t | hatmathssfs_t-k(W_2), mathbsfu_Omega)\\ &= h(mathssfs_t | W_2, mathbsfu_Omega) where and follows from the following Markov property. &W_1 rightarrow hatmathssfs_t-k(W_1) rightarrow \mathssfs_t, mathssfu_Omega\\\ &W_2 rightarrow hatmathssfs_t-k(W_2) rightarrow \mathssfs_t, mathssfu_Omega\ and follows from and~ and follows from the fact that sigma^2_t-k(W_1)le sigma^2_t-k(W_2) implies that fracE_1alpha^2_1 le fracE_2alpha^2_2 Thus the only difference between~ and~ is that the variance of the independent noise component in the first term is smaller in the former. Clearly we obtain a better estimate of mathssfs_t in~, which justifies the inequality in~. Eq.~ can be established as an immediate consequence of~. Since the noise mathssfz_t in the test channel is Gaussian and independent of all other random variables, we have Var(mathssfu_t|W_j, mathbsfu_Omega ) = Var(mathssfs_t|W_j, mathbsfu_Omega ) + sigma^2_z where the notation Var(mathssfa|W) indicates the noise variance of estimating mathssfa from W.
